blocks.md: Build reliability above an unreliable link. With only one unacknowledged packet at a time, the protocol needs a sequence bit, a checksum, an acknowledgement, and a retransmission timer.

blocks.label: FIG 1
blocks.caption: Loss or corruption leaves the sender waiting. When its timer fires, it retransmits the same packet; the receiver discards duplicates but repeats the ACK.

blocks.title: Duplicates are normal
blocks.md: An ACK can be lost after the receiver already delivered the data. The retry must be acknowledged again but never delivered twice. Sequence state makes that distinction.

blocks.label: What you implement
blocks.code:
func NewSender(cfg contract.Config) contract.Endpoint
func NewReceiver(cfg contract.Config) contract.Endpoint

blocks.input:
send DATA(seq=0, "abc")
receiver delivers and sends ACK(0)
ACK(0) is lost
timer fires
blocks.output:
resend DATA(0)
receiver delivers nothing
receiver sends ACK(0) again
blocks.explain: The repeated sequence tells the receiver this payload was already committed. Reliability requires idempotent handling on both sides, not merely retrying.

items: Copy application and packet payloads; never retain caller-owned slices.
Verify packet size and checksum before changing protocol state.
Keep at most one unacknowledged data packet and one timer in this tier.
Deliver every source byte exactly once and in order before reporting Done.

items.title: Make the clean path explicit
items.md: Chunk data, attach sequence and checksum, then wait for the matching ACK.

items.title: Treat every fault as an event
items.md: Loss means no callback, corruption means discard, duplication means repeat the previous response.

items.title: Finish both roles
items.md: EOF still needs protocol confirmation so sender and receiver agree the byte stream is complete.

blocks.title: Read the score as overhead
blocks.md: Completion ticks measure waiting; transmitted bytes, packet count, and retransmissions measure how much extra work reliability required; state bytes price the protocol memory.
